newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan June consumer prices up 1.84 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan June consumer prices up 1.84 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's consumer price index rose 1.84 percent in June compared to June 1996, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Saturday.
The June wholesale price index was down 1.62 percent compared to a year earlier, the directorate said.
The June CPI increase came in slightly above an average forecast for a 1.7 percent rise that was compiled from a Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists published on Thursday.
The directorate attributed the relatively high June CPI growth to torrential rains and floods that hit the island in June, especially early in the month, damaging crops.
In month-on-month terms, June CPI was up 1.69 percent from May, it said.
The poor June weather drove vegetable prices up an annual 18.98 percent and 35.51 percent from May, the directorate said.

More broadly, food prices rose 4.78 percent month-on-month due mainly to the spiking vegetable prices and the stabilisation of pork prices, which had slumped badly in March and April due to an islandwide outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease.
In the first six months, Taiwan's CPI grew 1.37 percent year-on-year, still falling into the directorate's estimate of 2.01 percent for whole 1997 CPI growth.
On the wholesale level, the June wholesale price index was up 0.79 percent from May, and the directorate attributed the rise to similar reasons as for the CPI rise.

The directorate forecast that vegetable prices would remain high in July as torrential rains have continued to buffet much of the island's farm areas in early July. Many vegetable farms that were damaged in June have not had the needed three-week recovery period to restore their output.
Vegetable prices account for only three percent of the total CPI weighting, it said.
The directorate estimated the June rains caused total losses of T$1.62 billion .

It said a three percent salary raise given to government employees from July 1 would add T$21.2 billion to state costs in the coming fiscal year. The raise would have virtually no impact on 1997 or 1998 CPI growth, the agency said.
